description: Find the largest real-post assignment among popular matchings for a bounded one-sided strict preference instance.

source.title: Popular Matchings
source.reuse: Algorithmic characterization only; input contract, fixtures, references, and ports are clean-room. The SIAM article retains its publisher copyright.

input.preference_list_lengths: Each length is in 1..P. Rows list distinct acceptable zero-based post IDs in strict best-to-worst order; posts have no preferences and do not vote.
input.last_resorts: A private last resort P+a is appended below every listed post for applicant a. It is used only to make the matching applicant-complete and is excluded from the returned cardinality.

output.meaning: Maximum number of real posts assigned in a popular applicant-complete matching; zero means no popular matching exists.
output.maximum_result_derivation: A matching uses at most min(A,P) real posts, with both A and P at most 6. Any popular assignment must cover a nonempty first-choice-post set, so zero is reserved for nonexistence.

algorithm_profile.source_model: One-sided strict preference lists: only applicants vote, and each list contains a nonempty strict ordering of an acceptable subset of posts.
algorithm_profile.primary: For each applicant compute f(a), the first post, and s(a), the first listed post not chosen first by any applicant, or that applicant's private last resort if no such post exists. In the reduced graph retain f(a) and s(a). Let A1 contain applicants whose s(a) is a last resort and A2 the rest. Build an applicant-complete A2 matching by repeatedly forcing the lowest-ID degree-one post, deleting its unique applicant and post, then matching each residual 2-regular component as an alternating cycle. If fewer residual posts than applicants remain, return zero. Augment real reduced-graph edges from unmatched A1 applicants in increasing applicant order, exploring post IDs ascending. Assign remaining A1 applicants to their private last resorts, then promote the lowest-ID f-applicant to any still-unmatched f-post in ascending post order.
algorithm_profile.independent: Enumerate each applicant's two theorem-permitted choices f(a) and s(a), reject collisions on real posts, and accept only assignments covering every f-post. Return the largest real-post count; this checks the characterization by assignment enumeration rather than the primary's forced-edge/cycle/augmentation procedure.
algorithm_profile.tie_policy: Input rows are strict. Degree-one posts, applicants, posts in DFS, and final promotions use ascending IDs. For a residual cycle, start from its smallest applicant and assign it the lower-ID of its two posts, then alternate around the cycle.

complexity.primary_time: O(A*(A+P)) for repeated degree-one reductions, residual cycle traversal, and bounded augmenting searches; A,P<=6

workspace.meaning: Fixed strict preference rows, reduced-choice arrays, post degrees, cycle and augmentation state.
